sections.h2: How can you sell a house fast in Yorktown, New York?
sections.html:
You can list the house, sell it privately, or accept a cash offer from a buyer who purchases it as it is. Yorktown is a town on the northern edge of Westchester County, about 38 miles north of midtown Manhattan, and its sellers deal with the town's tax receiver, assessor and building inspector rather than a city department.

The town is made up of five business hamlets, and no train runs inside its borders. Buyers weigh commute time, school district and the age of the systems in the house, so the paperwork you can hand over early tends to decide how fast a closing happens.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Yorktown homes?
sections.html:
Yorktown is mostly owner-occupied, with high incomes and values. The Census Bureau puts the July 1, 2025 estimate at 35,944 residents, a drop of 1.7 percent from the 2020 base of 36,562.

About 94.6 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, so many owners have been in place a long time. The mean commute is 37.7 minutes, and the nearest Metro-North stations are in Katonah on the Harlem Line and Peekskill on the Hudson Line.

sections.h2: Where is Yorktown, and what are its hamlets?
sections.html:
The town borders Putnam Valley in Putnam County to the north, Somers on the east, New Castle on the south and Cortlandt on the west. It covers 39.3 square miles, and about 36.8 of them are land. The Croton River runs through the southern part of the town, and it was dammed there to give New York City its first major clean water supply.

The area was called Hanover until 1788, when the township was incorporated as Yorktown to honor the 1781 victory at Yorktown, Virginia. Population jumped from 4,731 in 1950 to 16,453 in 1960 and reached about 36,000 by 2000, and it has barely moved since.

  • Yorktown Heights, the mailing address of Town Hall.
  • Jefferson Valley, home to the Jefferson Valley Mall.
  • Shrub Oak, Mohegan Lake and Crompond, with part of Crompond lying in Cortlandt.

Large employers and landmarks include the IBM Thomas J. Watson Research Center in the Kitchawan area and the headquarters of PCSB Bank in Yorktown Heights. Franklin D. Roosevelt State Park and the North County Trailway, on the old New York and Putnam rail bed, are the best-known open spaces.

Four districts reach into the town, and the tax bill depends on which one your house is in. The Yorktown Central School District covers most of the town. Lakeland Central, Croton-Harmon Union Free and Ossining Union Free districts cover the rest.

The town tax receiver collects school tax for all four districts, so the district named on your bill is the one that matters when a buyer asks. Confirm it before you list.

sections.h2: How do Yorktown winters and storms affect an older house?
sections.html:
The weather record at Yorktown Heights shows about 50.3 inches of precipitation a year and 39.5 inches of snow, with a January average low of 16.7 degrees and a record low of minus 15. The record high is 100.

Heavy snow loads, freeze and thaw cycles and long cold stretches put the roof, the driveway and the heating system at the top of an inspector's list. An older house here that has had its furnace and roof updated will show better than one with receipts missing.

sections.h2: How do Yorktown property tax bills and penalties work?
sections.html:
The Receiver of Taxes collects all taxes levied by the town, including fire, parks, sewer and water districts, plus county and school taxes. Owners get two bills a year, and the town says the bill is owed even if it never arrives.

  • School tax, covering July 1 to June 30: one bill mailed September 1 with two stubs. The first half is due September 30 and the second half January 31. A due date on a weekend moves to the next business day, which puts the 2027 second half on February 1.
  • School tax penalties on the first half: 2 percent in October, 5 percent in November, 7 percent in December and January, 10 percent in February and March, then 12 percent until sale.
  • Town and county tax: mailed April 1 and due by April 30 for the calendar year.
  • Town and county penalties: none in April, 2 percent in May, 5 percent in June and July, 7 percent in August and September, 10 percent from October to December, and 12 percent after that until sale.

The second half of school tax carries no penalty through January, then 10 percent in February and March. The town says no reminder notices go out in January and it cannot waive penalties. Mailed payments need a real United States Post Office postmark by the due date, and the town warns that postmarks now reflect when mail is first processed at a regional facility, so mail early. The Tax Office at 363 Underhill Avenue is open 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. on weekdays, and there is an after-hours drop box behind Town Hall.

sections.h2: How do you grieve a Yorktown assessment?
sections.html:
Grievance applications are accepted from June 1 until Grievance Day, the third Tuesday in June. For the 2027 roll the deadline is 8 p.m. on June 15, 2027, and the Board of Assessment Review meets at Town Hall that evening from 4 to 8 p.m. Filing costs nothing and needs no attorney.

Bring sales of similar houses in your neighborhood and school district from within a year of the July 1, 2026 valuation date, or an appraisal. Email applications are not accepted, but you can deliver in person, mail, use FedEx or UPS, or leave it in the drop box at the rear entrance of Town Hall. The board mails its decisions on September 15, 2027.

The assessor also reviews every property transfer, including buyer, seller and price. Standard exemptions include senior citizens, STAR, veterans and agricultural. Call 914-962-5722, extension 2, with questions.

sections.h2: What does the Yorktown Building Department require?
sections.html:
The Building Inspector enforces the town's zoning ordinance and the State building codes, issues permits and certificates of occupancy, and can condemn unsafe buildings. The 2025 editions of the New York State codes took effect on December 31, 2025, and applications filed on or after that date are judged under them. The department keeps weekday hours from 7:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. at Town Hall.

The town warns that it never asks anyone to wire a development fee. Fees are paid by check made out to the Town of Yorktown under its master fee schedule.

sections.h2: How do you record a Yorktown deed, and what transfer tax applies?
sections.html:
Deeds are recorded by the Westchester County Clerk's Land Records Division. The clerk's office requires a recording cover page, Form TP-584, Form RP-5217 and a payment cover page, all created in its PREP system. It also says a deed must be recorded in the county where the property lies.

The state tax is $2 for every $500 of price, with the price rounded up to the next $500. At the median owner-occupied value of $606,800, that rounds to $607,000 and yields $2,428. The tax is due when the deed is presented. A buyer of a residence at $1 million or more pays an extra 1 percent.

faqs.q: When is the second half of the Yorktown school tax due?
faqs.a: It is due January 31. When that date falls on a weekend, payment is accepted the next business day, so the 2027 second half is due by Monday, February 1.

faqs.q: What is the Yorktown penalty if I pay the town and county tax in June?
faqs.a: The penalty is 5 percent. The town and county bill is due April 30, adds 2 percent in May, then 5 percent in June and July, and the town says it cannot waive any penalty.

faqs.q: How do I contest my Yorktown assessment?
faqs.a: File a grievance application with the Assessment Office between June 1 and Grievance Day, the third Tuesday in June, which is June 15, 2027. Include supporting sales or an appraisal, and do not email it.

faqs.q: Which Yorktown office handles certificates of occupancy?
faqs.a: The Building Department at Yorktown Town Hall, 363 Underhill Avenue. The Building Inspector issues permits and certificates of occupancy and enforces zoning and State codes.

faqs.q: How much transfer tax would a $606,800 Yorktown sale generate?
faqs.a: The state tax is $2,428. The price rounds up to $607,000, which is 1,214 units of $500 at $2 each, and the seller pays unless the contract says otherwise.
